questions.question: If you need to brake while in a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
Brake as hard as you would on a straight road.
Wait until you leave the curve before braking.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans in a curve, the tires have less grip than when the motorcycle is upright. Try to straighten your motorcycle before braking. If you must brake while turning, brake slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: When you are about to pass another rider on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the right side of your lane so they can see you in their side mirror.
Move to the left side of your lane to see better ahead.
Stay in the center of your lane so they can see you in their rearview mirror.
Weave back and forth in your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the left side of your lane to see better ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane to see ahead better and be more visible to other drivers in the passing lane. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for traffic before you change lanes.

questions.question: If you need to both brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action first, then the other.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to do only one action.
Do not swerve and use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you need to brake and swerve, do these actions separately, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: Rounded mirrors on most motorcycles:

options.text: Are easy to get used to right away.
Make cars look closer than they really are.
Show only a narrow view of the road.
Make cars look farther away than they really are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make cars look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Rounded mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you than flat mirrors. However, they make objects appear farther away than they actually are. Practice judging distances with rounded mirrors until you get used to them.

questions.question: If you need to swerve, what should you do?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Push the handlegrip in the direction you want to turn.
Push the handlegrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handlegrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, push the handlegrip gently in the direction you want to go. To turn left, push the left handlegrip, then push the right to straighten out. To turn right, push the right handlegrip, then the left.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Avoid sudden movements.
Use only the front brake to slow down or stop.
Use both brakes to slow down or stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake to slow down or stop.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, use both brakes, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden movements. Watch for oily spots, dirt, gravel, shade, and bridges, as these areas are often more slippery.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you from behind, which part of your lane should you use?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder.
Use the left portion of your lane.
Use the center portion of your lane.
Use the right portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, the center of your lane is the safest position. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may cause the driver to turn back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: When you are following a car, which part of the lane should you ride in?

options.text: The left portion.
The center portion.
The right portion.
The left or right portions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane when following a car so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position helps them see you better.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while you are braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the brake until the tire grips again, then brake again.
Release the brake and use only the front brake.
Keep the brake locked until you stop completely.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the brake locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while braking, do not release the brake. Keep it locked until your motorcycle comes to a complete stop.

questions.question: When you park a motorcycle next to a curb, how should you position it?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Like a car, with both wheels the same distance from the curb.
At the left edge of the space so approaching drivers can see it better.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb with the rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: On a long trip, you should:

options.text: Take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine or other stimulants if you feel sleepy.
Wear warm clothes to stay comfortable during the ride.
Ride more than 12 hours in a single day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear warm clothes to stay comfortable during the ride.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on a long trip, dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day and take a rest break at least every two hours. Do not use caffeine or other stimulants because you will feel very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you on your left, you should:

options.text: Move as far right as possible to help the other driver.
Move to the shoulder to help the other driver.
Stay in the center of your lane.
Stay in the left part of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. Moving toward the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Moving toward the far side may cause the other driver to pull back too soon. The center position is safest.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always stay in the same part of your lane.
Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Only ride in the center of the lane for visibility.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to get drivers' attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Move your position as needed based on changing road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: A rectangular sign can be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that inform drivers of road rules, such as speed limits, are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn by turning only your head and eyes. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance. Bend your arms slightly when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: Studies show that most riders in crashes:

options.text: Don't brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.
Brake the front tire too much and don't brake the rear tire enough.
Only use the front brake.
Only use the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.
questions.explanation: Most riders in crashes don't brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.

questions.question: Small vehicles can look ______ away and seem to move ______ than they really are.

options.text: Farther, slower
Farther, faster
Closer, slower
Closer, faster

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther, slower
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles can appear farther away and seem to be moving slower than they actually are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge the vehicle's real distance and speed.

questions.question: To prevent fatigue on a long ride, you should do all of the following except:

options.text: Dress warmly.
Limit the distance you travel each day.
Take frequent rest breaks.
Take artificial stimulants.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take artificial stimulants.
questions.explanation: To reduce fatigue on long rides, dress to protect yourself from wind and rain. Ride no more than about six hours per day and rest at least once every two hours. Do not take artificial stimulants because you will feel very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes.
Don't use the brakes, just downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes if you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn the other driver.
Speed up.
Pull over to the side of the road.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn the other driver.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, flash your brake light before slowing down. The tailgater may be focused on you and not notice other hazards that require slowing traffic.

questions.question: Your riding clothes should protect you from all of the following, except:

options.text: Sunburn.
Windburn.
Chapped lips.
Dehydration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Chapped lips.
questions.explanation: Riding clothes should protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, dehydration, cold, and motorcycle parts. Good clothing also helps protect you if you crash.

questions.question: What is the best protection for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: A cushion of space between their vehicle and other vehicles.
A good leather jacket.
Sturdy boots.
A good understanding of motorcycle laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: A cushion of space between their vehicle and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid crashes is to keep distance between your motorcycle and other vehicles. This gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. Wearing proper gear is also important.

questions.question: Riders wearing helmets are ________ more likely to survive a crash than those without helmets.

options.text: Two times
Three times
Eight times
Ten times

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet makes you three times more likely to survive a head injury in a crash, regardless of your speed.

questions.question: When being passed, you should not move to the far edge of your lane because it:

options.text: Discourages the passing driver from cutting into your lane too early.
Encourages the passing driver to cut into your lane too early.
Encourages the passing driver to complete the pass as quickly as possible.
Encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourages the passing driver to cut into your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far edge of your lane could encourage the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: Of crashes between motorcycles and cars, how many are caused by car drivers failing to yield right-of-way?

options.text: About 10 percent
About 25 percent
Over 50 percent
About 90 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: Over 50 percent
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car crashes happen because car drivers fail to yield right-of-way to riders.
